newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 24.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- Industrial holdings company Malbak announced the sale of two interests for a total of 350 million rand, bringing the conglomerate to the final stages of unbundling.

- President Mobutu Sese Seko returned to the forefront of Zaire's political stage when he received a letter from President Nelson Mandela which sought to end the war with rebels fighting for the overthrow of the Zairean government.

- Stricter measures against defaulting local authorities and individual electricity users are starting to pay off for Eskom, with an estimated 1.3 billion rand owed to the parastatal expected to be reduced this year.

- In one of the first major initiatives to deliver mass low-cost housing, the National Housing Finance Corp has unlocked housing finance for 118,000 families through the approval of credit facilities totalling 116 million rand to four housing lenders.
- The National Party government had considered establishing a "third force" in 1985 and 1986 to deal with political unrest and counter-insurgency, former president F.W. de Klerk said.
- The Commission for Conciliation, Mediation and Arbitration has been flooded with more than 10,000 referrals over the past few months, many of which should not have been sent to it.
BUSINESS REPORT

- Ingwe, the world's largest steam coal exporter, is considering expanding its South American coal assets by buying the soon-to-be privatised El Cerrejon mine in Colombia -- the largest open-cast mine in the world.
- More than 25 percent of TDK audio tapes sold in South Africa are counterfeit, according to Frank & Hirsch, the official licensee in the country.

- Millions of South Africans, especially those living in rural areas, will now be able to afford to tune in their favourite radio programmes thanks to a drop in duties on radios, according to Derrick Sturgess, managing director of BayGen Power Group, maker of a wind-up radio.

- An agreement between the KWV wine cooperative and members of the Cape Wine and Spirit Institute should pave the way for deregulation of the Cape wine industry, with massive ramnifications for the rapidly growing distilling industry in South Africa, an industry source said.

- The Nederburg wine auction produced record wine sales of 4.4 million rand, with the price of red wine rising 30 percent and some retailers saying they would be forced to increase imports to meet the price demands of local buyers.
SAKE-BEELD

- An annual salary and market review by Deloitte & Touche Executive Placements found South Africa continued to show a shortage of quality staff last year, mainly through the outflow of people emigrating because of uncertainty in the country.
- South Africa's banking industry faces a difficult year, according to Viv Bartlett, chairman of the Council of South African Banks (Cosab).
- The cabinet has approved restructuring of the electricity distribution industry.
- The National Housing Finance Corp is in talks with two major banks to cooperate in the launch of new mortgage bond initiatives for the poorer sections of the population.
- Cementation Mining has begun work on a surface drilling contract valued at 50 million rand in the Target and Sun prospecting area of the Free State province.
- Gencor has decided not to take a leading role in the management of the Brazilian Companhia Vale do Rio Doce project.
- The Association of Unit Trusts said the new money market trusts would not be announced on April 1 as expected and are likely to be made known on May 2, because of unforeseen circumstances.
THE STAR
- Big business is returning to Johannesburg's inncer city after years of crime and grime reduced investor confidence to an all-time low.
- National Party leader F.W. de Klerk has launched a scathing attack on the Truth and Reconciliation Commission, accusing it of bias.

- Deputy President Thabo Mbeki returned from Kinshasa optimistic over the chances of peace after a brief meeting with Zairean president Mobutu Sese Seko, to whom he delivered a message from President Nelson Mandela.
